overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated Shorts shows extreme divergence in audience pull. First-person experiential 'What If You Fell Into...' hooks combined with extreme, hostile cosmic environments generated the channel's highest viewership (800–1,050+ views) and peak engagement (up to 3.7% like ratio and comment activity). Conversely, abstract psychology trivia ('Fake Memories', 'Song Stuck in Head') and duplicate uploads of basic biology/space facts ('Octopus Hearts', 'Silent Space') stagnate under 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Hazard 'What If You Plunged/Fell' Simulation Hook
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) outperformed third-person declarative trivia by over 500%.
winning_patterns.action: Frame extreme science and geography topics around direct sensory immersion ('What happens to your body the second you drop in...').

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos exploring surreal, violent conditions ('Burning Ice', 'Liquid Diamond', 'Darker Than Coal', 'Supersonic Rubies') consistently crossed 700–1,050 views.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor scripts around mind-bending tactile contradictions (e.g., oceans of liquid methane, raining titanium, crushing gravitational depths).

weak_patterns.evidence: Uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined at 5–53 views, while repeated 'Songs Stuck in Your Head' averaged under 50 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt generic psychology and brain trivia until distinct narrative storytelling can be integrated.

weak_patterns.pattern: Duplicate Video Reposting Without Conceptual Iteration
weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple redundant uploads of 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' (34 to 220 views) and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' suffered severe algorithmic suppression.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict uniqueness rules; test fresh entities and unexplored phenomena rather than recycling identical hooks.
